question.text: How many turkey poults will USDA NASS report as net placed in the United States during October 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the October 2026 net poult placements figure published in USDA NASS's [Turkey Hatchery](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery) report scheduled for release at 3:00 p.m. ET on November 13, 2026. Use the value for October 2026 in the report's net poult placements table for the United States (total all breeds), which NASS publishes in thousands of poults; for example, a reported figure of 19,571 thousand poults resolves as 19,571. The figure as first published in that report governs, and revisions published in later NASS reports do not change the resolution. If the report does not include an October 2026 placement estimate, resolution waits for the next NASS report that contains it.
question.fine_print:
- Use NASS's published estimate as-is, including all breeds; do not adjust it for exports, deaths in transit, or any other factor.
- The other figures in the same report (turkey eggs in incubators on November 1, poults hatched in October, percentages of a year earlier) are context only and are not the resolution value.
- Only the October 2026 placement figure counts, not the September or November estimates or the November 1 eggs-in-incubators value.

research:
Nothing has settled this yet. The October 2026 figure first appears in the November 13 report. On the primary data, October 1 eggs in incubators (26,695) times the last three years' egg-to-placement ratios (0.778 to 0.815) gives about 20,800 to 21,750 thousand. I'm passing that along as context, not as a forecast.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-13: The newest Turkey Hatchery release is the October 13, 2026 report. The next two are scheduled for 2026-11-13 and 2026-12-14. [ESMIS](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery)
- 2026-10-13: The net placements table shows September 2026 at 19,571 thousand (102% of 19,096). The October 2026 cell is blank. The October 2025 comparison value now reads 21,284. [tkha1026.txt](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796103/tkha1026.txt)
- 2026-10-13: Other figures in that report:
  - Eggs in incubators on October 1: 26,695 (102% of 26,122).
  - September hatch: 21,122.
  - Revised August 2026 placements: 21,164 (first published as 21,213).
  - Revised September 1 eggs: 24,814 (first published as 25,174).
  
  [tkha1026.txt](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796103/tkha1026.txt), [tkha0926.txt](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796058/tkha0926.txt)
- Reliability: the root mean square error for placements is 4.2% (90% confidence interval ±7.1%). The average gap between first and latest estimates is 678 thousand, the largest 1,775 thousand. Over the last 24 months, 14 first estimates came in below the latest figure and 9 above.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The number first appears on 2026-11-13.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-10-30 (from the question background, which I did not verify): APHIS reports 11 commercial flocks confirmed in 30 days, including turkey flocks in North Dakota, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Iowa.
- My searches turned up no 2026 coverage or outlook specific to turkey placements. The HPAI analysis I found dates from 2025, when HPAI and avian metapneumovirus (aMPV) shrank poult supply. [FoodMarket](https://www.foodmarket.com/News/A/1301148/ANALYSIS-Turkey-Poult-Supply-Shrinks-in-2025)

## 4. Base rates
October placements (latest revised values, thousands):

| Year | Sept placements | Oct placements | Sept to Oct change | Oct 1 eggs in incubators | Oct placements / Oct 1 eggs | Oct placements / Oct hatch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 19,091 | 20,895 | +9.4% | (not recorded) | n/a | 0.922 |
| 2024 | 18,030 | 19,510 | +8.2% | 25,083 | 0.778 | 0.926 |
| 2025 | 19,096 | 21,284 | +11.5% | 26,122 | 0.815 | 0.926 |

Sources: [tkha0925.txt](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/k643b117x/m326p167w/76539164w/tkha0925.txt), [tkha1026.txt](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796103/tkha1026.txt)

- Applying the 2023 to 2025 September-to-October step (+8% to +11.5%) to 19,571 gives about 21,140 to 21,820.
- Applying the egg ratio (0.778 to 0.815) to 26,695 gives about 20,770 to 21,760.

**First prints can differ a lot from revised values.** Because of the 2025 shutdown, NASS did not publish October or November 2025 reports; the listing jumps from September 12 to December 15, 2025. The December 2025 report first printed:
- October 2025 placements at **19,684**, later revised to 21,284 (+8%).
- September 2025 at 18,179, later revised to 19,096.
- October 2025 hatch at 21,410, later revised to 22,981.
- October 1, 2025 eggs at 25,461, later revised to 26,122.

So the "21,284" comparison is a revised figure; the first print was much lower. More recent revisions have been small (August 2026: 21,213 to 21,164). [tkha1225.txt](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/795687/tkha1225.txt), [ESMIS listing](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery?page=1)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold, and no expert forecast, on turkey poult placements. The markets supplied (Vermont milk, maple syrup, corn yield, and markets about the country Turkey) do not match this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-13, 3:00 p.m. ET: Turkey Hatchery release, which resolves the question. [ESMIS](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery)
- Ongoing: APHIS HPAI confirmations in turkey-belt states. October placements are already over, so new detections can only affect what hatcheries report, not the actual number.
- Possible: a shutdown or other disruption that delays the release. That happened in 2025.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 11 days. The figure is released November 13, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. ET.

(b) The latest known value is September 2026 net placements of 19,571 thousand, from the October 13, 2026 report. Other inputs:
- October 1 eggs in incubators: 26,695 thousand, up 2% year over year.
- October 2025 placements: 21,284 thousand (revised).

(c) If nothing changed from September, the figure would be about 19,600. That is unrealistic, because October is seasonally higher.

(d) Three trend-based estimates:
- Applying the usual September-to-October step of +8% to +11.5% gives about 21,150 to 21,800.
- Applying the year-over-year trend (+2%) to October 2025 gives about 21,700.
- Applying the ratio of placements to October 1 eggs gives about 20,800 to 21,750.

A central estimate is about 21,400.

(e) Historical variation:
- NASS's root mean square error for placements is 4.2%.
- Seasonal step sizes vary by about ±2 percentage points.
- The first-print revision noise is now small, as with August 2026 (21,213 first printed, revised to 21,164).
- A plausible standard deviation is about 550 to 650 thousand.

(f) I found no markets or expert forecasts. Using the egg and hatch data as the implicit consensus points to about 21,000 to 21,700.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: HPAI control-area restrictions in Minnesota, the Dakotas and Wisconsin cause widespread deferred placements, possibly combined with aMPV losses. Hatcheries then dump or export poults, and placements print near 19,500 to 20,000.
- High: unaffected growers front-load placements to cover depopulated supply. Together with a strong hatch from the high egg set, that pushes placements to about 22,500 or more.

The late-October HPAI detections mostly came after most October placements were made, so I apply only a slight downward tilt.

(a) **Time left:** about 11 days. The figure is first published at 3:00 p.m. ET on November 13, 2026.

(b) **Latest known value:** September 2026 net placements were 19,571 thousand (Oct 13, 2026 report). That is up 2% year over year. October 1 eggs in incubators were 26,695 thousand, also up 2% year over year. October 2025 placements, revised, were 21,284 thousand.

(c) **If nothing changed:** carrying the September level forward gives about 19,600. That is not realistic, because October is seasonally a peak month.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- Year over year: applying the +2% trend to October 2025 gives about 21,700.
- Seasonal step: applying the 2023 to 2025 September-to-October step (+8% to +11.5%) gives 21,140 to 21,820.
- Eggs in incubators: the egg-to-placement ratios give 20,770 to 21,760.
- Hatch route: implied October hatch of about 23,400, times the usual 0.926 placement-to-hatch ratio, gives about 21,700.

Two things pull the number down from there:
- First prints have tended to come in below later revised values (14 of the last 24). September 1 eggs were just revised down by 360.
- The October HPAI losses in Minnesota, North Dakota, Wisconsin and Iowa may defer some placements.

Taking these together, I centre the forecast near 21,250.

(e) **Historical variation:** NASS's root mean square error for placements is 4.2%, about 900 thousand. October levels over 2023 to 2025 ranged from 19,510 to 21,284. Recent first-to-revised changes have been small, though the shutdown-affected October 2025 first print was revised up by 8%.

(f) **Experts and markets:** I found no relevant markets or expert forecasts. The structural estimates cluster around 20,800 to 21,800.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** HPAI control-area movement restrictions and depopulations in Minnesota and the Dakotas cause widespread deferred placements. The first-print survey also undercounts, as happened in December 2025. Placements come in near 19,000 to 19,500.
- **High:** unaffected producers restock aggressively to fill holiday and early-2027 demand, and the hatch converts fully. Placements come in near 22,800 to 23,300.
